facts.claim: GLib GOption uses a table of option entries to drive parsing.
facts.source_quote: 1. **[GLib GOption / GOptionContext](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/goption.html)** is the closest documented fit. A table of option entries drives parsing and help generation in one call. Short and long names, both `--name=value` and `--name value`, and positional collection are documented. String and filename array option types collect repetitions; callbacks provide a route for custom aggregation or overriding. The [unknown-option setting](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/method.OptionContext.set_ignore_unknown_options.html) explicitly leaves ignored options in `argv`. Its caveat matters for forwarding: the parser cannot reliably decide whether a separate non-option value belongs to an unknown option. Choose a clear forwarding boundary or convention. The API uses ordinary C tables and functions, though GLib adds a substantial dependency. The [official overview](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/index.html) identifies LGPL-2.1-or-later licensing; Windows-specific command-line handling is documented. Native subcommands and exact scalar overwrite semantics were not verified.
